_comment: Hand-written descriptions for the Blam console reference at /docs/console.
The release build ships every function's help pointer as null, so console.json
carries names and signatures but not purposes. Entries here are merged by name
by hub/scripts/sync-console-defs.mjs; a name with no entry renders with its
signature alone, so add what you know and leave the rest.
Keep each entry to one or two sentences about what the function does when it
runs. Whether it runs at all in this build (425 are compiled out) comes from

families.script: The HS language itself: the special forms that sequence and branch scripts, the arithmetic and comparison operators, the sleep family, casts between object types, and printing. Everything else in the table is the engine API these forms call into.
families.ai: Placing, commanding and querying AI: squads, encounters, orders, awareness, vehicles and the actor state the campaign scripts drive.
families.cs: Command scripts: the per-actor movement and behaviour sequences that scripted set pieces are built from. Most take the script's own actor as an implicit subject.
families.unit: Bipeds and vehicles as units: health, shields, seats, weapons, emotions and the animations a scripted unit plays.
families.player: The local players: their units, effects, input, training text and the flags that gate campaign progress.
families.cinematic: Cinematic mode, letterboxing, scripted cameras and the title cards and screen effects that cutscenes use.
families.object: Scenario objects in general: creation and destruction by name, teleporting, scaling, damage and the object lists the scripts iterate.
families.game: The game session: saving and reverting checkpoints, difficulty, co-op state, winning and losing, and the tick counters.
families.survival: Firefight: waves, rounds, sets, bonus rounds and the scoring that goes with them.
families.chud: The in-game HUD: showing and hiding its parts, objectives and chapter titles on screen, and training prompts.
families.debug: Debugging aids. Most of these are compiled out of the release build and answer without doing anything.
families.sound: Playing and stopping sound tags, looping sounds, music and the mixer classes.
families.net: Networking: the session, hosting, and the counters a network game exposes to scripts.
families.objectives: Mission objectives as shown on the HUD: showing, finishing and clearing them by index.
families.camera: Scripted cameras: taking control from the player, moving between points and the camera modes.
families.render: Rendering switches: clip distances, lighting and effect toggles, most compiled out of the release build.
families.device: Devices: doors, lifts, switches and machines, driven by position and power from 0 to 1.
families.events: The engine's event log and its display, largely compiled out of the release build.
families.vehicle: Vehicles as containers: loading and unloading seats, hovering and the vehicle-specific state.
families.mp: Multiplayer game state exposed to scripts.
families.cui: The UI screen stack: opening, closing and querying screens by name.
families.controller: Controller profiles and settings as the scripts read them.
families.tag: Tag loading and reloading at runtime.
families.simulation: The deterministic simulation: its tick, its state and its debugging counters.
families.flock: Flocks: the ambient creatures spawned in groups.
families.volume: Trigger volumes: testing objects and players against them, and teleporting the ones outside.
families.cheat: The classic cheats. Every one of them is compiled out of this build: the engine accepts the name and does nothing.
families.console: Commands that belong to the console itself rather than the engine. The MJOLNIR mod answers `help` on its own, from this same table.
families.meteorite: Functions 343 added for Halo Campaign Evolved, recognisable by their capitalised names. None appear in the classic engines.
families.other: Prefixes with too few members for a page of their own.
families.skull: Skulls, switched from the console with skull_enable and read back with skull_enabled. All four functions are live, and this is the shipped route to most of what the compiled-out cheats did: skull_bandanna is bottomless ammo and grenades, and the counter turns to the infinity sign the moment it is enabled. The skull argument must be one of these names (the compiler lists them when given anything else; the list it prints is cut off after skull_leadhead, so there may be a few more): skull_iron, skull_black_eye, skull_tough_luck, skull_catch, skull_fog, skull_famine, skull_thunderstorm, skull_tilt, skull_mythic, skull_assassin, skull_blind, skull_superman, skull_birthday_party, skull_daddy, skull_red, skull_yellow, skull_blue, skull_angry, skull_bandanna, skull_bonded_pair, skull_boom, skull_envy, skull_eye_patch, skull_foreign, skull_ghost, skull_grunt_funeral, skull_jacked, skull_malfunction, skull_masterblaster, skull_pinata, skull_recession, skull_scarab, skull_so_angry, skull_swarm, skull_thats_just_wrong, skull_they_come_back, skull_boots_off_the_ground, skull_adaptation, skull_reload, skull_spore_visibility, skull_night_vision, skull_lights_out, skull_riskrun, skull_pop, skull_armistice, skull_fragile, skull_give_and_take, skull_stow_and_grow, skull_hip_fire, skull_temperamental, skull_floor_is_lava, skull_magnified, skull_johnny_ammo_tree, skull_leadhead.

functions.begin: Evaluates each expression in order and returns the value of the last.
functions.begin_random: Evaluates the expressions in a random order.
functions.if: Evaluates the second expression if the condition is true, otherwise the optional third.
functions.cond: Evaluates the first result whose condition is true.
functions.set: Assigns a value to a global variable.
functions.sleep: Pauses the current script for the given number of simulation ticks.
functions.sleep_forever: Pauses the current script, or the named one, until something wakes it.
functions.sleep_until: Pauses the current script until the condition is true, re-testing it every so many ticks.
functions.wake: Wakes a sleeping script by name.
functions.print: Prints a string to the console.
functions.inspect: Prints an expression's value to the console.
functions.unit: Casts an object to a unit.
functions.vehicle: Casts an object to a vehicle.
functions.weapon: Casts an object to a weapon.
functions.device: Casts an object to a device.
functions.players: A list of every player's unit.
functions.object_create: Creates the named scenario object if it does not already exist.
functions.object_create_anew: Creates the named scenario object, replacing any existing one.
functions.object_teleport: Moves an object to a cutscene flag.
functions.object_set_scale: Scales an object to the given size over the given number of ticks.
functions.object_hide: Hides or shows an object without destroying it.
functions.objects_attach: Attaches one object to another at the named markers.
functions.objects_detach: Detaches an object attached with objects_attach.
functions.ai_place: Places the named squad or encounter, optionally with a given number of actors.
functions.ai_kill: Kills the named AI immediately, with death effects.
functions.ai_erase: Removes the named AI from the game without death effects.
functions.ai_erase_all: Removes every AI from the game.
functions.ai_magically_see: Makes the AI aware of the given unit as if it had seen it.
functions.ai_living_count: The number of living actors in the named squad or encounter.
functions.ai_set_orders: Gives the named squad the named orders.
functions.ai_enable: Turns AI updating on or off.
functions.unit_get_health: A unit's health as a fraction from 0 to 1.
functions.unit_get_shield: A unit's shield as a fraction from 0 to 1.
functions.unit_enter_vehicle: Puts a unit into the named seat of a vehicle.
functions.unit_exit_vehicle: Makes a unit leave its vehicle.
functions.unit_set_emotional_state: Sets a unit's emotional state by name, which changes its animations.
functions.vehicle_load_magic: Loads the given units into a vehicle's seats without animation.
functions.vehicle_unload: Unloads the named seat of a vehicle.
functions.device_set_position: Moves a device to a position from 0 (closed) to 1 (open).
functions.device_set_power: Sets a device's power from 0 to 1; an unpowered device does not move.
functions.game_save: Requests a checkpoint at the next safe moment.
functions.game_save_no_timeout: Requests a checkpoint and waits as long as it takes for a safe moment.
functions.game_won: Ends the level as a win.
functions.game_lost: Ends the level as a loss.
functions.game_difficulty_get: The difficulty the game was started on.
functions.game_is_cooperative: Whether more than one player is in the game.
functions.fade_in: Fades the screen in from the given colour over the given number of ticks.
functions.fade_out: Fades the screen out to the given colour over the given number of ticks.
functions.cinematic_start: Enters cinematic mode: hides the HUD and hands the camera to the script.
functions.camera_control: Takes control of the camera for scripts (true) or gives it back to the player (false).
functions.camera_set: Moves the camera to a cutscene camera point over the given number of ticks.
functions.objectives_show: Shows the objective with the given index on the HUD.
functions.objectives_finish: Marks the objective with the given index complete.
functions.chud_show: Shows or hides the whole HUD.
functions.chud_show_shield: Shows or hides the shield bar.
functions.chud_show_motion_sensor: Shows or hides the motion sensor.
functions.chud_show_screen_objective: Puts an objective string on screen.
functions.chud_show_screen_chapter_title: Puts a chapter title on screen.
functions.volume_test_object: Whether an object is inside a trigger volume.
functions.volume_test_objects: Whether any object in the list is inside a trigger volume.
functions.volume_test_objects_all: Whether every object in the list is inside a trigger volume.
functions.volume_teleport_players_not_inside: Teleports any player outside the trigger volume to the flag.
functions.sound_impulse_start: Plays a sound tag at an object, at the given volume.
functions.sound_impulse_stop: Stops a sound started with sound_impulse_start.
functions.sound_looping_start: Starts a looping sound at an object, at the given volume.
functions.cheat_all_vehicles: Spawns one of every vehicle near the player.
functions.cheat_teleport_to_camera: Teleports the player to the camera's position.
functions.help: Lists functions and globals whose names contain the given text, with signatures.
functions.skull_enable: Turns a skull on or off. Verified live: `skull_enable skull_bandanna true` gave bottomless ammo at once. Takes a skull name from the list on this page, not a bare word.
functions.skull_enabled: Whether the named skull is on.
functions.skull_affects_players: Whether the named skull applies to players, or only to AI.
functions.game_rate: Sets the simulation rate: 1 is normal, 0.5 is half speed. The second and third arguments are ramp and duration in seconds as far as testing shows; `game_rate 0.5 0 30` put the game in slow motion, and `game_rate 1 0 0` restores it. This is the live replacement for the game_speed global, which has no storage in this build.
functions.game_tick_get: The simulation tick counter. It advances about sixty times a second and keeps advancing at that rate under game_rate, so it measures real time, not game time.

globals.cheat_infinite_ammo: Weapons never run out of ammunition.
globals.cheat_jetpack: Holding jump keeps the player airborne.
globals.cheat_medusa: AI dies as soon as it sees the player.
globals.cheat_omnipotent: Every shot the player fires kills.
globals.cheat_chevy: Vehicles run like they used to.
globals.console_pauses_game: Opening the console pauses the simulation.
